_readme: Frozen pre-release predictions vs actuals. scripts/backtest.py --freeze <quarter> writes a prediction BEFORE a release; afterwards fill each metric's `actual` (and optionally `lean`/`actual_direction`) by hand, add the quarter to data/gpi-history.json, and re-run scripts/backtest.py so the comparison becomes a new data point.

street_estimate.note: vendor-reported consensus for the Oct 28, 2026 print; secondary source

metrics.label: Used same-store retail units, YoY %
metrics.method: persistence (no indicator model beat the naive baselines in leave-one-out testing)

metrics.label: Used same-store retail GPU, YoY %
metrics.method: persistence (no indicator model beat the naive baselines in leave-one-out testing)
metrics.range_basis: seasonal-ratio benchmark (Q2->Q3 ratios from prior years)

metrics.label: New-vehicle same-store GPU, YoY %
metrics.method: persistence (no indicator model beat the naive baselines in leave-one-out testing)

metrics.label: Adjusted diluted EPS ($)
metrics.method: seasonal-ratio benchmark (Q2->Q3 EPS ratios 2023-2025, mean); indicators have no demonstrated skill on EPS
metrics.range_basis: min/max of the three prior-year Q2->Q3 ratios (2023, 2024, 2025)

forecasts.note: Prediction frozen BEFORE the release. After GPI reports, fill `actual` for each metric (same units as `predicted`: YoY % for same-store metrics, $ for EPS) and add the quarter to data/gpi-history.json, then re-run scripts/backtest.py.
